subject: Re: DPA - roles, telemetry, embeddings & subprocessors
messages:
From: Jonathan Welsh <jon.welsh@acmemedical.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@acmemedical.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: DPA redline + questions on roles/telemetry/embeddings

Soojin —

Thanks for sending a first pass of the DPA. I attached our redline (ACME_DPA_redline_v3.pdf) — most comments are around one bucket of questions we need clarification on before our GC signs:

1) Controller vs. processor: For embeddings derived from our customer content, do you consider Redwood the processor (acting on our instructions) or would you assert any controller status for that derived data? We need this spelled out explicitly.

2) Telemetry/logs: Your platform collects usage logs and telemetry. Are those treated as separate data types from customer content? Do you process telemetry as a controller (for platform improvement) or as a processor on our behalf? If telemetry is used for model training/quality, we need an opt-out path.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: Please provide the current subprocessor list and confirm whether any subprocessors store embeddings outside the US (SCCs, EU transfers).

4) Retention & deletion: We need confirmation that embeddings and underlying content can be deleted and that you support API-driven deletion with contractual retention limits.

We circled/highlighted specific clauses in the redline. If you can address these points and send a clean DPA or DocuSign-ready version, that would speed exec. Can we get responses by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
Jonathan Welsh
Senior Counsel — Acme Medical
[jon.welsh@acmemedical.com]

[attachment: ACME_DPA_redline_v3.pdf (PDF)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jonathan Welsh <jon.welsh@acmemedical.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redline + questions on roles/telemetry/embeddings

Jonathan — thanks for the clear redline and callouts. Looping Laura (our Head of Legal) to confirm precise contract language — below are quick answers to the bullets while Laura and team prep a revised DPA: 

- Controller vs Processor: For customer-provided content (including embeddings derived from that content), Redwood acts as a processor and processes that data strictly on your instructions. We will not assert independent controller rights over customer content or embeddings created from it.

- Telemetry/Logs: Operational telemetry (aggregated usage metrics, system logs, perf traces) is currently processed by Redwood to run and improve the service. We treat that telemetry as platform data used for diagnostics and product improvement. We understand the sensitivity and can:
  * Provide a contractual commitment to limit telemetry use for model training;
  * Offer pseudonymization and an opt-out for telemetry retention beyond operational needs for customers under enterprise agreements.

- Subprocessors & Transfers: I'll attach our current subprocessor list. We use subprocessors for monitoring, storage, and cloud infrastructure. For EU transfers we support SCCs (we can provide a signed annex) and can discuss onshore processing for embeddings where required.

- Deletion & Retention: We offer an API for deletion of customer content and associated artifacts (including embeddings). We will align retention language with your data retention schedule and provide runtime confirmation when deletions complete.

I'll let Laura share suggested redline language and the DocuSign flow. Happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer — I can make time Thursday afternoon PST.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonathan Welsh <jon.welsh@acmemedical.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redline + questions on roles/telemetry/embeddings

Jonathan —

Thanks for the redline. I’ve reviewed and attached a counter-redline that: (1) explicitly states Redwood is processor for customer content and embeddings derived from that content, (2) carves out operational telemetry and provides limited controller-level processing rights strictly for platform stability/monitoring, and (3) adds an explicit prohibition on using customer-provided content or customer-specific embeddings to train models for third-party customers without prior consent.

Key proposed language (high level):
- "Processor scope: Redwood will act solely as Processor with respect to Customer Content, including features and artifacts derived exclusively from Customer Content (e.g., embeddings)."
- "Telemetry: Redwood may collect and process operational telemetry necessary to provide and secure the Service. Telemetry will be pseudonymized by default and shall not be used to improve or train public models on a customer-by-customer basis absent explicit written consent. Customer may request an expanded telemetry opt-out in writing for enterprise agreements."
- "Deletion: Redwood will provide API-driven deletion for Customer Content and associated derivatives, with contractual retention limits and confirmation of deletion events."

Requested follow-ups from Acme: please confirm whether you need all subprocessors listed in an annex (we can provide) or an access-controlled register. Also confirm whether you require onshore (US-only) storage for embeddings or SCCs for EU customers.

Attached: redline_for_review.docx and a short redline_summary.xlsx that maps the requested changes to our proposed text.

If these edits look acceptable, we can produce a clean DPA and send via DocuSign for signature.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

[attachment: redline_for_review.docx (Word)]
[attachment: redline_summary.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Jonathan Welsh <jon.welsh@acmemedical.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@acmemedical.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redline + questions on roles/telemetry/embeddings

Laura —

Appreciate the detailed response and the proposed language. A couple of follow-ups before we proceed to signature:

1) The clause preventing use of customer-specific embeddings for model training is helpful. Can we make that explicit: "Customer Content and Customer-Specific Embeddings will not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve any public or shared models without Customer's prior written consent."

2) Telemetry opt-out: Acme will take the enterprise telemetry opt-out for model training. Please confirm how that opt-out is implemented operationally and whether it impacts platform support (e.g., we accept a potential loss of fine-grained debugging data).

3) Subprocessors: please provide the full annex of subprocessors and a timeline for notifying us of new subprocessors (we typically require 30 days' notice unless emergency).

If you can incorporate these clarifications into the clean copy, we should be able to sign. Please send the DocuSign link once ready — target: our GC signs by Friday, 20 Feb.

Thanks,
Jonathan

[No attachments]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: DPA redline + questions on roles/telemetry/embeddings

Jonathan — great, thanks. Laura will update the clean copy with the exact sentence on embeddings and explicit telemetry opt-out implementation notes. We will also attach the subprocessor annex and include a 30-day notification clause for non-emergency additions.

Next steps:
- Laura: finalize clean DPA and include the requested sentence on embeddings and the telemetry opt-out operational note.
- Ops: prepare subprocessor annex and a short note on how telemetry opt-out is enforced (pseudonymization + flag to exclude data from training pipelines).
- I will upload the clean DPA to DocuSign and send the execution link to you by EOD Thursday. Our expected sign flow: Acme GC signs, then Redwood Countersign via DocuSign within 48 hours.

If that timeline works, I’ll send the DocuSign link when ready. Thanks again for the quick turnaround.

Best,
